authors.bio: Communications consultant Peter Hammar specializes in helping high technology companies reach their increasingly diverse market segments. His background includes broadcasting, instructional media, technical writing, and exhibit planning and trade show work. Hammar is a member of the Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers, currently serving as Chairman of the San Francisco Section. He has also served on national SMPTE committees, including the 1989 23rd Annual Television Conference, for which he was Program Chairman. He is a member of the Audio Engineering Society and has been a frequent featured speaker at conventions and meetings in the U.S. and in Europe. In addition to his communications activities, Hammar is active in preserving the history of this industry. He created the Ampex Museum of Magnetic Recording in Redwood City, California. He helped found “Save Entertainment Technology” (SAVET) in Burbank, California, a non-profit service dedicated to increasing the number and quality of exhibits on audio and video technical history in museums around the world. He is also a co-founder of the Music Performance Research Centre in London, a nonprofit copyright protection and archival service organization.
